description: Unified 40-Scenario End-to-End Agent Reasoning Benchmark: 30 Quantitative Symbolic Calculation & Delegation Scenarios + 10 Statutory RAG Grounding Scenarios

scenarios.title: Class R Flat Fee Accrual (45 Days, Actual/365)
scenarios.prompt: Audit the management fee accrual for Lux Alpha SICAV Class R: the Gross Asset Value (GAV) is 75,000,000 EUR for an accrual period of 45 calendar days. Under Section 9.1 and Section 9.2 (Actual/365) of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, calculate the exact management fee accrual in EUR.

scenarios.title: Day-Count Convention Penalty Audit (Actual/360 vs Actual/365)
scenarios.prompt: An administrator computed the quarterly management fee for Lux Alpha SICAV Class R on a GAV of 100,000,000 EUR for 90 days using Actual/360 instead of Actual/365. Under Section 9.1 and Section 9.2 of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, compute the exact fee under both day-count conventions and quantify the exact administrator overstatement in EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Actual/360: 300,000.00 EUR; Actual/365: 295,890.41 EUR; Overstatement: 4,109.59 EUR.

scenarios.title: Class H-USD Currency Hedged Fee Accrual (60 Days in USD)
scenarios.prompt: Under Section 9.1 and Section 9.2 of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, calculate the exact management fee accrual for Class H-USD on a Gross Asset Value (GAV) of 60,000,000 USD accrued over 60 calendar days under the Actual/365 convention.

scenarios.title: Cash Dividend Accrual on Ex-Dividend Date per Fund Share
scenarios.prompt: Under Section 8.1 of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, cash dividends declared on equity holdings must be accrued in the fund's receivables on the Ex-Dividend Date. A sub-fund has 2,500,000 shares outstanding. On the Ex-Date, the fund accrues a declared dividend of 1.45 EUR per share on 500,000 shares of holding Alpha, and 0.85 EUR per share on 800,000 shares of holding Beta. Calculate the total dividend receivable in EUR and the exact NAV receivable impact per fund share.

scenarios.title: Class I vs Class R Subscription Tax Rate Discrepancy (91 Days)
scenarios.prompt: Audit the quarterly subscription tax (taxe d'abonnement) accrual for Lux Alpha SICAV on 30 June (91 accrual days under Actual/365): Class I GAV is 200,000,000 EUR and Class R GAV is 80,000,000 EUR. The administrator mistakenly applied the retail rate (0.05%) to both classes, booking 34,904.11 EUR. Using Section 9.1 of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, compute the exact tax for Class I (0.01%), Class R (0.05%), the correct combined EUR total, and quantify the administrator's overstatement.
scenarios.rubric: Class I: 4,986.30 EUR; Class R: 9,972.60 EUR; Total: 14,958.90 EUR; Overstatement: 19,945.21 EUR.

scenarios.title: Multi-Class Currency Segregation in Tax Audit (EUR vs USD)
scenarios.prompt: Under Section 9.1 and Section 9.2 (Actual/365) of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, compute the quarterly subscription tax for a 92-day period across three share classes: Class I with GAV of 150,000,000 EUR, Class R with GAV of 50,000,000 EUR, and Class H-USD with GAV of 40,000,000 USD. State each class tax in its native currency, the combined EUR-only sub-total, and confirm whether USD tax is segregated.
scenarios.rubric: Class I: 3,780.82 EUR; Class R: 6,301.37 EUR; Class H-USD: 5,041.10 USD; EUR Subtotal: 10,082.19 EUR.

scenarios.title: Annualized Ongoing Charges Load & Basis Point Audit
scenarios.prompt: Audit the annual ongoing charges for Lux Alpha SICAV Class R on an average GAV of 120,000,000 EUR over a full 365-day year: management fee is 1.20% p.a., subscription tax is 0.05% p.a., custody fee is 0.03% p.a., and administration/audit fees are 0.04% p.a. Compute the exact EUR amount for each expense category, the total annual ongoing charges in EUR, and the total expense load in basis points.
scenarios.rubric: Total: 1,584,000.00 EUR; Expense load: 1.32% or 132 bps.

scenarios.title: Leap Year Day-Count Impact Audit (Actual/365 vs Actual/366)
scenarios.prompt: For an institutional fund with a flat management fee rate of 0.40% p.a. on a GAV of 300,000,000 EUR accrued over a 91-day quarter, calculate the exact management fee under Actual/365 versus Actual/366 (leap year convention), and quantify the exact difference in EUR.

scenarios.title: Class I Tiered Fee Accrual on 180M GAV (Footnote (*1) Breakpoint)
scenarios.prompt: Audit the quarterly management fee accrual for Lux Alpha SICAV Class I for a 91-day period (Actual/365) on a Gross Asset Value (GAV) of 180,000,000 EUR. Applying Section 9.1 and Footnote (*1) of the Prospectus (0.40% on first 50M EUR, 0.30% on excess), calculate the Tier 1 fee, Tier 2 fee, and total Class I fee in EUR.

scenarios.title: Administrator Tier Omission Audit on 650M GAV (92 Days)
scenarios.prompt: Audit the management fee accrual for Lux Alpha SICAV Class I on a GAV of 650,000,000 EUR over 92 days (Actual/365). The fund administrator booked 655,342.47 EUR by applying a flat 0.40% rate across the entire GAV. Using Section 9.1 Footnote (*1), compute the correct tiered fee for Tier 1 (first 50M @ 0.40%) and Tier 2 (600M @ 0.30%), the correct total fee, and quantify the administrator's overstatement in EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Correct: 504,109.59 EUR; Overstatement: 151,232.88 EUR.

scenarios.title: Combined Class I & Class R Multi-Class Tiered Fee Audit (75 Days)
scenarios.prompt: Calculate the management fee accrual for Lux Alpha SICAV over 75 calendar days (Actual/365) where Class I GAV is 400,000,000 EUR and Class R GAV is 150,000,000 EUR. Apply Footnote (*1) tiered rates to Class I (0.40% on first 50M, 0.30% on remaining 350M) and the flat 1.20% rate to Class R. Compute the exact fee for each class and the combined total fee in EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Class I: 256,849.31 EUR; Class R: 369,863.01 EUR; Total: 626,712.32 EUR (or 626,712.33 EUR unrounded).

scenarios.title: 3-Tier Hurdle Fee Schedule Simulation (182 Days)
scenarios.prompt: A specialized fund mandate specifies a 3-tier annual management fee: Tier 1 is 0.50% on the first 100,000,000 EUR; Tier 2 is 0.35% on the next 200,000,000 EUR (between 100M and 300M EUR); and Tier 3 is 0.20% on any portion exceeding 300,000,000 EUR. For a GAV of 450,000,000 EUR over an accrual period of 182 days (Actual/365), calculate the exact fee for each of the three tiers and the total fee in EUR.

scenarios.title: Standard 5/10/40 Concentration Exposure Test (Fully Compliant)
scenarios.prompt: A Luxembourg UCITS has total Net Assets of 500,000,000 EUR. It holds transferable securities in 5 corporate issuers: Issuer A = 48,000,000 EUR, Issuer B = 45,000,000 EUR, Issuer C = 42,000,000 EUR, Issuer D = 35,000,000 EUR, and Issuer E = 20,000,000 EUR. Under Article 52(1) and 52(2) of UCITS Directive 2009/65/EC, calculate the exact percentage exposure of each issuer, identify which holdings exceed the 5% threshold, calculate the aggregate exposure of the >5% basket, and verify if the 40% ceiling is breached.

scenarios.title: Active Breach of the 10% Single-Issuer Limit
scenarios.prompt: A Luxembourg UCITS with Net Assets of 320,000,000 EUR holds 28,800,000 EUR (9.00%) in Issuer X. The portfolio manager actively purchases an additional 6,400,000 EUR of Issuer X securities. Calculate the new total holding in EUR, the new percentage exposure, the excess over the 10% statutory ceiling in EUR and basis points, and state whether Circular CSSF 24/856 grants any tolerance threshold for active breaches.
scenarios.rubric: New holding: 35,200,000.00 EUR (11.00%); Excess: 1.00% / 100 bps / 3,200,000.00 EUR; 0 bps tolerance.

scenarios.title: Breach of the 40% Aggregate Basket with Borderline Holdings
scenarios.prompt: A UCITS fund has Net Assets of 250,000,000 EUR. Its holdings are: Issuer 1 = 24,000,000 EUR, Issuer 2 = 22,500,000 EUR, Issuer 3 = 21,000,000 EUR, Issuer 4 = 19,000,000 EUR, Issuer 5 = 17,500,000 EUR, and Issuer 6 = 12,000,000 EUR. Under Article 52(2) of Directive 2009/65/EC, calculate the percentage of each holding, identify which holdings exceed 5.00%, calculate the aggregate percentage of the >5% basket, and quantify the breach over the 40.00% ceiling in EUR and percentage.

scenarios.title: Article 52(3) Covered Bonds 25% Limit and 80% Aggregate Cap
scenarios.prompt: A UCITS invests in covered bonds (bonds issued by credit institutions subject to special public supervision per Article 52(3) of Directive 2009/65/EC). Fund Net Assets are 400,000,000 EUR. Holdings: Bank A = 92,000,000 EUR, Bank B = 88,000,000 EUR, Bank C = 84,000,000 EUR, Bank D = 76,000,000 EUR. Calculate each bank's percentage against the 25% single-issuer limit, the aggregate sum of these investments, and evaluate compliance against the 80% aggregate limit under Article 52(3).
scenarios.rubric: Aggregate: 85.00% > 80.00% ceiling; Breach: 5.00% (500 bps) / 20,000,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: NAV Pricing Error Variance Audit + Table 9 REA Reporting Thresholds
scenarios.prompt: On 2025-04-15, an Equity UCITS has Replicated Net Assets of 150,000,000 EUR with 1,200,000 shares outstanding, while the Fund Administrator reported a NAV per share of 126.80 EUR. Total investor compensation is 48,000 EUR and the single largest investor compensation is 6,200 EUR. Perform the full quantitative audit: calculate the exact replicated NAV per share, the absolute EUR variance, the relative variance in bps, compare against the CSSF 24/856 Table 1 Equity threshold (100 bps), and determine under Table 9 whether a Separate Report or a full-scope Special Report by the REA is triggered.
scenarios.rubric: Rep NAV: 125.00 EUR; Rel Variance: 144.00 bps (or 141.96 bps); Triggers Special Report (single comp 6,200 > 5,000).

scenarios.title: Accounting Method Investment Breach Loss & Indemnification Audit
scenarios.prompt: Under Circular CSSF 24/856 Section 5.5.3 (Accounting Method), audit the indemnification for an active investment breach: a portfolio manager purchased 50,000 unauthorized shares of Company Z at 120.00 EUR per share (total cost 6,000,000 EUR), incurring 15,000 EUR in acquisition transaction fees. To rectify the breach, 30,000 shares were sold at 112.00 EUR per share incurring 10,000 EUR in disposal fees, and 20,000 shares remain in the portfolio at a valuation price of 108.00 EUR per share. Compute the realized loss, unrealized loss, direct transaction costs, and total indemnification payable to the fund.
scenarios.rubric: Realized: 240k; Unrealized: 240k; Direct costs: 25k; Total: 505,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: Swing Pricing Dilution Factor & Fund Benefit Audit
scenarios.prompt: A fund with unswung Net Asset Value of 250,000,000 EUR across 1,000,000 shares (unswung NAV = 250.00 EUR per share) applies swing pricing with a threshold of 3.00% of NAV and a swing factor of 40 bps (0.40%). On Valuation Day T, subscriptions total 12,000,000 EUR and redemptions total 3,000,000 EUR. (1) Calculate the net capital flow as a percentage of NAV and determine if swing pricing is triggered. (2) Compute the swung NAV per share. (3) Compute the number of shares issued to subscribing investors at the swung NAV. (4) Calculate the total dilution adjustment amount in EUR retained by the fund.
scenarios.rubric: Net flow: 3.60% > 3.00%; Swung NAV: 251.00 EUR; Benefit: 35,856.57 EUR (net) or 47,808.76 EUR (gross).

scenarios.title: Comprehensive Dual-Regime Bitemporal Multi-Class Liability & REA Audit
scenarios.prompt: On 2024-12-10 (Event Date), Lux Alpha SICAV Class I had GAV of 480,000,000 EUR and Class R had GAV of 120,000,000 EUR. For a 70-day accrual period, the fund administrator booked management fees using Actual/360 and omitted the Footnote (*1) tiered reduction on Class I (booking a flat 0.40% on Class I and 1.20% on Class R). The error was detected on 2025-02-15 (Detection Date). (1) Calculate the correct Class I fee under Actual/365 with Footnote (*1) tiering (50M @ 0.40%, 430M @ 0.30%). (2) Calculate the correct Class R fee under Actual/365. (3) Calculate the administrator's booked fees under Actual/360 for both classes. (4) Compute the total administrator overstatement in EUR. (5) State which circular governs reporting on the Detection Date and whether this error triggers an REA report under CSSF 24/856 Table 9/11.
scenarios.rubric: Correct: 561,917.80 EUR (or 561,917.81 EUR); Overstatement: 91,415.53 EUR > 50,000 EUR -> Special Report.

scenarios.title: CSSF 02/77 Money Market NAV Pricing Error & Exemption Threshold Audit
scenarios.prompt: On 2024-08-15, a Luxembourg Money Market UCI (cash fund) under Circular CSSF 02/77 has Replicated Net Assets of 200,000,000 EUR with 1,000,000 shares outstanding, while the Administrator published a NAV of 200.70 EUR per share. The resulting total investor prejudice is 22,000 EUR, but the single largest investor suffered a prejudice of 2,800 EUR. (1) Calculate the replicated NAV per share, absolute EUR variance, and relative variance in bps. (2) Determine whether the variance exceeds the CSSF 02/77 Money Market tolerance threshold (25 bps). (3) Under Section I.3 of Circular CSSF 02/77, determine whether the fund is exempt from submitting a full corrective action plan to the CSSF.
scenarios.rubric: Rep NAV: 200.00 EUR; Rel Variance: 34.88 bps (or 35 bps) > 25 bps; Single investor 2,800 > 2,500 -> Not exempt.

scenarios.title: UCITS Directive Article 52(5) Corporate Group 20% Concentration Cap
scenarios.prompt: A Luxembourg UCITS has total Net Assets of 300,000,000 EUR. It invests in transferable securities issued by three different subsidiaries belonging to the same banking group: Subsidiary A = 24,000,000 EUR, Subsidiary B = 21,000,000 EUR, and Subsidiary C = 27,000,000 EUR. (1) Calculate the percentage exposure of each subsidiary and verify if any single issuer exceeds the 10% limit under Article 52(1) of Directive 2009/65/EC. (2) Calculate the aggregate exposure to this corporate group. (3) Determine whether Article 52(5) (20% group ceiling) is breached, and quantify the breach in percentage, basis points, and EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Subs < 10%; Group aggregate: 24.00% (72M EUR); Breach: 4.00% (400 bps) / 12,000,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: UCITS Directive Article 55 Fund of Funds (Single UCI & Non-UCITS Cap)
scenarios.prompt: A UCITS fund of funds has Net Assets of 100,000,000 EUR. It allocates capital across four target funds: Target UCITS 1 = 18,000,000 EUR, Target UCITS 2 = 15,000,000 EUR, Target Non-UCITS UCI Alpha = 17,000,000 EUR, and Target Non-UCITS UCI Beta = 16,000,000 EUR. (1) Calculate the percentage allocation to each target fund and verify compliance with the Article 55(1) 20% single-fund ceiling. (2) Calculate the aggregate exposure to Non-UCITS target funds. (3) Evaluate compliance against the Article 55(2) 30% aggregate non-UCITS limit, and quantify any breach in percentage and EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Single funds <= 20%; Non-UCITS aggregate: 33.00% (33M EUR) > 30% ceiling; Breach: 3.00% (300 bps) / 3,000,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: UCITS Directive Article 83 Temporary Cash Borrowing Limit (10% Cap)
scenarios.prompt: To meet massive quarter-end redemption requests without selling illiquid assets, a Luxembourg UCITS with Net Assets of 180,000,000 EUR draws down a temporary bank credit facility of 21,600,000 EUR. Under Article 83(2)(a) of Directive 2009/65/EC, calculate the borrowing ratio as a percentage of Net Assets, verify whether the statutory 10% temporary borrowing ceiling is breached, and quantify the excess borrowing in percentage, basis points, and EUR.
scenarios.rubric: Borrowing ratio: 12.00%; Statutory cap: 10.00%; Excess: 2.00% (200 bps) / 3,600,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: CSSF 24/856 Section 5.5.3 Accounting Method vs Economic Method Indemnification
scenarios.prompt: Under Circular CSSF 24/856 Section 5.5.3, audit an active investment breach: a portfolio manager purchased 100,000 unauthorized shares at 50.00 EUR per share (5,000,000 EUR total cost), paying 10,000 EUR in acquisition fees. Upon discovery, the fund sold all 100,000 shares at 46.00 EUR per share (4,600,000 EUR gross proceeds), incurring 12,000 EUR in disposal fees. Over the same holding period, the fund's official benchmark index fell by 10.00%. (1) Compute the total indemnification payable under the standard Accounting Method (realized loss + all direct transaction costs). (2) Compute the theoretical fund outcome under the Economic Method if the 5,000,000 EUR had tracked the benchmark index (-10%), and compare the difference. (3) State whether the fund management company can unilaterally apply the Economic Method without a pre-existing documented policy.
scenarios.rubric: Accounting indemnity: 422,000.00 EUR; Economic Method outperformance: 78,000.00 EUR; Policy required.

scenarios.title: High-Water Mark (HWM) Performance Fee Accrual (Lux Alpha Class P)
scenarios.prompt: Audit the annual performance fee for Lux Alpha SICAV Class P: the sub-fund has 800,000 shares outstanding and charges a 15% performance fee subject to a High-Water Mark (HWM) of 150.00 EUR per share. At the financial year-end, the Gross NAV before performance fee is 162.00 EUR per share. Under Section 9.3 of the Prospectus, calculate the outperformance per share, the performance fee per share, the total performance fee accrual in EUR, and the final Net NAV per share after fee deduction.
scenarios.rubric: Outperformance: 12.00 EUR/share; Fee/share: 1.80 EUR (12 * 0.15); Total fee: 1,440,000.00 EUR; Net NAV: 160.20 EUR/share.

scenarios.title: Anti-Dilution Liquidity Levy on Large Inflow Subscriptions
scenarios.prompt: Under Section 8.3 of the Lux Alpha Prospectus, when daily net subscriptions exceed 10,000,000 EUR, an anti-dilution liquidity levy of 25 basis points (0.25%) is applied to incoming cash and retained directly in the fund's capital to protect existing shareholders from portfolio rebalancing costs. An institutional investor submits a subscription order of 16,000,000 EUR. Calculate the exact levy amount in EUR credited to the fund, the net amount invested into fund shares, and the total cash received by the fund.

scenarios.title: UCITS Commitment Approach Global Exposure & Derivatives Netting
scenarios.prompt: Under CSSF Circular 11/512 and Article 51 of UCITS Directive 2009/65/EC, a fund using the Commitment Approach has Net Assets of 120,000,000 EUR. The fund holds three derivative positions: Position 1 is long equity index futures with notional value of 35,000,000 EUR; Position 2 is short single-stock equity futures of 20,000,000 EUR eligible for hedging netting; Position 3 is an interest rate swap with duration-adjusted net commitment of 18,000,000 EUR. Calculate the net equity commitment in EUR, the total global commitment exposure in EUR, the global exposure percentage against Net Assets, and the remaining headroom under the 100% statutory ceiling.
scenarios.rubric: Net equity: 15M; Total commitment: 33,000,000.00 EUR; Ratio: 27.50%; Headroom: 72.50% / 87,000,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: Multi-Currency Share Class Net Asset & FX Loss Allocation
scenarios.prompt: Lux Alpha SICAV has pool Net Assets of 210,000,000 EUR comprising two share classes: Class I (EUR) representing 65.00% of assets (136,500,000 EUR) and Class H-USD (hedged) representing 35.00% (73,500,000 EUR equivalent, valued at 79,380,000 USD at FX 1.0800). A portfolio trading loss of 2,100,000 EUR occurs. Under Section 9.1 and Section 9.2, calculate the proportional loss allocated to Class I in EUR, the loss allocated to Class H-USD in EUR, the loss converted to USD at 1.0800, and the updated net assets for both classes.
scenarios.rubric: Class I loss: 1,365,000.00 EUR; Class H-USD loss: 735,000.00 EUR / 793,800.00 USD; New Class I: 135,135,000.00 EUR.

scenarios.title: Late Investor Compensation Statutory Interest Audit (Law of 29 April 1999)
scenarios.prompt: Following a material NAV calculation error, a former investor was owed 45,000 EUR in compensation. Payment was delayed by 180 calendar days beyond the mandatory 30-day settlement deadline. Under the Law of 29 April 1999 and Luxembourg commercial interest rules, the statutory legal interest rate is 5.00% p.a. (Actual/365). Calculate the exact statutory interest amount in EUR, the total payout due to the investor, and state whether this interest can be charged to the fund assets.
scenarios.rubric: Statutory interest: 45,000 * 0.05 * 180 / 365 = 1,109.59 EUR; Total: 46,109.59 EUR; Zero charge to fund.

scenarios.title: Bitemporal Regime Transition: CSSF 02/77 vs CSSF 24/856 Chapter 10
scenarios.prompt: A Luxembourg Bond UCITS experienced a 60 bps NAV calculation error on 15 November 2024 (Event Date), but the error was only uncovered on 20 January 2025 (Detection Date). Cross-referencing Circular CSSF 02/77 (Section I.2) and Circular CSSF 24/856 (Chapter 10 and Table 1): (1) Compare the bond fund materiality tolerance thresholds between both circulars; (2) Explain which circular governs the substantive threshold and calculation of prejudice on the Event Date versus the procedural notification requirements on the Detection Date.
scenarios.rubric: Substantive threshold on Event Date (2024) is governed by CSSF 02/77 (50 bps); Procedural notification and reporting on Detection Date (2025) follow CSSF 24/856 Chapter 10.

scenarios.title: Symmetrical Accounting Cost Methods for Active Investment Breaches
scenarios.prompt: Under Circular CSSF 24/856 Section 5.5.3 (Points 78 to 82), what are the permitted cost accounting methods (LIFO, FIFO, weighted average cost) when calculating the financial impact of active investment breaches, what principles govern their selection, and is switching between methods permitted mid-audit?
scenarios.rubric: Permitted methods are FIFO, LIFO, WAC; must follow fund accounting policy consistently; opportunistic switching prohibited.

scenarios.title: REA Statutory Intervention Scope: Table 10 vs Table 11 Comparison
scenarios.prompt: Under Circular CSSF 24/856 Section 8.4 (Paragraphs 150 and 151), contrast Table 10 (Investment Breaches) and Table 11 (Other Chapter 6 Breaches) regarding the statutory intervention of the réviseur d'entreprises agréé (REA). Under what financial conditions is a Special Audit Report required versus a Separate Summary Report?
scenarios.rubric: Table 10 covers investment breaches, Table 11 covers Chapter 6 errors; Special report required if total > 50k EUR or single investor > 5k EUR.

scenarios.title: Customized NAV Tolerance Limits & Point 35(d)(iii) 500 bps Absolute Cap
scenarios.prompt: Can a Luxembourg UCI Part II or SIF fund legally establish an internal NAV error tolerance threshold of 650 basis points (6.50%) in its constitutive documents under Circular CSSF 24/856 point 35(d)(iii)? What is the maximum statutory cap, and where must unclaimed indemnification for exited investors be deposited under the Law of 29 April 1999?
scenarios.rubric: 650 bps is impermissible; absolute statutory cap is 500 bps under point 35(d)(iii); unclaimed funds deposited with Caisse de consignation.

scenarios.title: Depositary Oversight Framework across UCITS Directive, Lux Alpha Prospectus, and CSSF 24/856
scenarios.prompt: Cross-reference the depositary oversight framework across UCITS Directive 2009/65/EC (Articles 22 and 24), the Lux Alpha SICAV Prospectus (Section 9.3 Depositary and Custody role), and Circular CSSF 24/856 (Section 8.1 and Chapter 7): (1) What are the depositary's statutory oversight duties regarding unit valuation and does custody delegation exonerate liability under the Directive? (2) How does the Lux Alpha Prospectus reflect the depositary's custody and safekeeping roles? (3) What mandatory reporting obligations are imposed on the depositary when an operational NAV calculation error occurs under Circular CSSF 24/856?
scenarios.rubric: Depositary must oversee NAV calculation under Directive Art 22/24 without liability discharge upon delegation; Lux Alpha Prospectus Sec 9.3 assigns safekeeping to Depositary Bank; CSSF 24/856 Section 8.1 requires depositary independent verification and reporting of material NAV errors.

scenarios.title: Closed-World Abstention Guard (Out-of-Corpus US SEC Rule 2a-5 & CIMA)
scenarios.prompt: Under the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (CIMA) Rule on Calculation of Asset Values for Regulated Mutual Funds and US SEC Rule 2a-5, what is the mandatory de minimis materiality threshold in basis points for daily NAV errors in crypto asset funds?
scenarios.rubric: Agent must explicitly abstain / state that US SEC Rule 2a-5 and Cayman CIMA are out of scope of the Luxembourg CSSF / UCITS corpus.

scenarios.title: Money Market Fund Materiality Threshold Evolution: CSSF 02/77 vs CSSF 24/856
scenarios.prompt: Compare the statutory NAV error materiality thresholds for Money Market UCIs (cash funds) between Circular CSSF 02/77 (Section I.2) and Circular CSSF 24/856 (Table 1). What was the historical threshold, what is the new threshold, and what is the regulatory intent behind the reduction?
scenarios.rubric: CSSF 02/77 threshold was 25 bps (0.25%); CSSF 24/856 lowered threshold to 20 bps (0.20%) to strengthen investor protection in cash funds.

scenarios.title: Evolution of Investment Breach Governance: UCITS Directive 2009/65/EC, CSSF 02/77, and CSSF 24/856
scenarios.prompt: Cross-examine the regulatory treatment of investment rule breaches across UCITS Directive 2009/65/EC (Article 52 5/10/40 diversification rules), Circular CSSF 02/77 (Section II), and Circular CSSF 24/856 (Chapter 5 and Table 10): (1) How are active vs passive breaches distinguished under UCITS rules? (2) What was the historical remediation and investor compensation principle under CSSF 02/77? (3) How does CSSF 24/856 formalize the compensation methodology and statutory REA audit intervention threshold?
scenarios.rubric: Active breaches require portfolio rectification and investor indemnification; passive breaches require priority rectification under market conditions; CSSF 02/77 established general restitution; CSSF 24/856 Chapter 5 establishes standardized accounting/economic formulas and Table 10 REA intervention limits.

scenarios.title: Prospectus Valuation Primacy & Statutory NAV Error Thresholds: Lux Alpha vs CSSF 24/856
scenarios.prompt: Cross-reference Section 8.1 and Section 8.3 of the Lux Alpha SICAV Prospectus with Circular CSSF 24/856 (Section 5.3 and Table 1): (1) What specific valuation methodology does Lux Alpha establish for listed securities and swing pricing adjustments? (2) How does Circular CSSF 24/856 regulate NAV calculation errors arising from incorrect asset valuation, and what tolerance threshold applies to equity funds under Table 1?
scenarios.rubric: Lux Alpha Prospectus Section 8.1 mandates closing market prices and Section 8.3 governs swing pricing; CSSF 24/856 Section 5.3 treats incorrect pricing as a NAV error with a 50 bps threshold for equity funds under Table 1.

scenarios.title: Same-Day Rectification CSSF Reporting Exemption (Point 42)
scenarios.prompt: Under Circular CSSF 24/856 Point 42, under what conditions is an investment fund management company completely exempt from formally notifying the CSSF and its réviseur d'entreprises agréé regarding an operational NAV calculation error?
scenarios.rubric: Exempt if error is detected and rectified on the same valuation day prior to NAV publication/dissemination and causes zero financial prejudice.
